shape_contract.hat: Starts its own stack. Nothing snaps above it. The rest of the stack runs when the event fires — it does not 'wait' inside another stack.
shape_contract.stack: A command. Snaps under a hat or another stack block and moves execution to the next block when it finishes. Blocks whose name starts with 'start' finish immediately and leave the motor/sound running.
shape_contract.boolean: A hexagon. Reports true/false. Does nothing on its own. Must be dropped inside wait-until, if, or repeat-until.
shape_contract.reporter: An oval. Reports a number or string. Must be dropped into a number/string slot. Does nothing on its own.
shape_contract.c: A C-shaped wrapper (forever / if / repeat). Holds a stack in its mouth.
shape_contract.cap: A stack that nothing can snap under (stop all).

python.code:
async def on_close():
    ...
# hats become tasks; or await runloop.until(lambda: distance_sensor.distance(port.D) < 100)

notes: HAT. Starts its own stack when the condition becomes true. It does not sit inside forever. Default value is 8, default unit percent (≈ 16 cm). If you wanted 'when something is close', this is the right *family*, but wait-until + isDistance is the version that lives inside a driving loop.
